newsitem.title: UK: United Utilities's Pitcher hangs on.
newsitem.headline: United Utilities's Pitcher hangs on.

text.p: United Utilities Plc, one of Britain's biggest water and electricity companies, left a boardroom battle over the future of its chairman Sir Desmond Pitcher unresolved on Tuesday despite calls for him to step down.

After an unscheduled board meeting following personality clashes between Sir Desmond and other directors, United said only it was aware of the succession issues and was "taking immediate action to resolve the position".
"There will be a further announcement in the Autumn," it stated. "In the meantime, the company do not intend issuing any further statement."

Institutional shareholders, led by Peter Middleton -- a non executive director and chairman of Barclays' investment banking unit BZW -- have been pressing for Pitcher to take over a non-executive role or quit the company's board altogether.

However, following the unexpected sacking last month of chief executive Brian Staples, speculation has intensified that Pitcher -- dubbed "King Des" by critics for what they call his autocratic management style -- would step down by the end of the year rather than see out his contract as a non-executive chairman.
Pitcher, one of the best-paid utility executives in the country, is due to retire in 2000.

After a two-hour board meeting, United said only it had received reports from Middleton and non-executive director Jane Newell on the views of institutional investors. A spokesman declined to comment further.
